sk-f0c708e7.stem: About how many bones are there in the adult human skeleton?
sk-f0c708e7.explanation: The adult skeleton has about 206 bones: 80 in the axial skeleton and 126 in the appendicular skeleton. In the newborn the number is around 270–300 because many parts have not yet fused.

sk-93d7b509.stem: Which is the longest and strongest bone of the body?
sk-93d7b509.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, heaviest and strongest bone of the body; it is about a quarter of a person's height.

sk-a3b15dfd.stem: Which is the smallest bone of the body?
sk-a3b15dfd.explanation: Of the three ossicles of the middle ear, the stapes is the smallest bone of the body; its footplate fits into the oval window.

sk-59a23a69.stem: Which membrane, rich in vessels and nerves, covers the outer surface of bone?
sk-59a23a69.explanation: The periosteum covers the outer surface of bone; cells of its inner layer allow the bone to thicken and fractures to heal. Joint surfaces have no periosteum and are covered by hyaline cartilage. The endosteum lines the marrow cavity.

sk-4df6a75a.stem: What is the shaft of a long bone called?
sk-4df6a75a.explanation: The shaft of a long bone is the diaphysis, its ends the epiphyses and the growth zone between them the metaphysis. Inside the diaphysis is the medullary cavity containing bone marrow.

sk-45e4abe2.explanation: Osteoclasts are multinucleated cells of monocyte origin that break down bone tissue. Osteoblasts build new bone, and osteocytes are mature cells embedded in bone.

sk-900539f3.stem: In which tissue are blood cells produced?
sk-900539f3.explanation: Blood cells are made in red bone marrow. In adults red marrow lies mainly in the flat bones (sternum, ribs, hip bone, vertebrae); the marrow in the shafts of long bones turns into fatty yellow marrow.

sk-6f3cbcfe.stem: Where do long bones grow in length?
options: In the middle of the shaft
sk-6f3cbcfe.explanation: Growth in length takes place in the epiphyseal plate of the metaphysis as cartilage cells multiply and ossify; the plate closes at the end of puberty. Growth in width occurs by the periosteum adding new bone.

sk-1a21cd83.stem: Which of the following bones belongs to the axial skeleton?
sk-1a21cd83.explanation: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column and thoracic cage (sternum and ribs). The clavicle and scapula belong to the shoulder girdle, the hip bone to the pelvic girdle and the humerus to the free upper limb.

sk-2db88c9e.stem: Which of the following is an example of a flat bone?
sk-2db88c9e.explanation: Flat bones are thin and broad (skull vault, sternum, ribs, scapula). The femur and metacarpals are long bones, the capitate a short bone and the vertebrae irregular bones.

sk-a98a93de.stem: Which of the following is NOT a sesamoid bone?
sk-a98a93de.explanation: Sesamoid bones develop within tendons: the patella, the pisiform, the sesamoids under the MP joints of the thumb and big toe and, in some people, the fabella. The lunate is a short bone of the proximal carpal row.

sk-66a08b42.stem: Which bone forms the forehead and the roof of the orbits?
sk-66a08b42.explanation: The frontal bone forms the forehead with its vertical squamous part and the roofs of the orbits and floor of the anterior cranial fossa with its horizontal orbital part.

sk-cb93516d.stem: Which is the only bone of the skull that moves at a synovial joint?
sk-cb93516d.explanation: The bones of the skull are firmly joined by sutures; the only movable joint is the temporomandibular joint between the mandible and the temporal bone.

sk-4559542c.stem: What are the unossified membranous areas between the skull bones of a newborn called?
sk-4559542c.explanation: Fontanelles are membranous areas where the sutures meet; they allow the head to mould during birth and the brain to grow. The largest is the anterior fontanelle.

sk-f341b2fb.stem: Between which bones is the sagittal suture?
options: Between the two halves of the frontal bone
sk-f341b2fb.explanation: The sagittal suture joins the two parietal bones in the midline. The coronal suture lies between frontal and parietal bones, the lambdoid between parietal and occipital, the squamous between parietal and temporal.

sk-bb6020cc.stem: How many bones take part in forming the orbit?
sk-bb6020cc.explanation: The orbit is formed by seven bones: frontal, zygomatic, maxilla, sphenoid, ethmoid, lacrimal and palatine.

sk-13d66ee5.stem: How many cervical vertebrae are there in the vertebral column?
sk-13d66ee5.explanation: The vertebral column has 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 3–5 coccygeal vertebrae.

sk-894f664c.stem: What is the special name of the first cervical vertebra (C1)?
sk-894f664c.explanation: C1 is called the atlas, C2 the axis and C7 the vertebra prominens. The atlas has no body and no spinous process.

sk-a8bb291d.stem: How many vertebrae fuse to form the sacrum?
sk-a8bb291d.explanation: Five sacral vertebrae fuse to form the triangular sacrum; the 3–5 coccygeal vertebrae below form the coccyx.

sk-d1d02687.stem: Which curvature of the spine develops when a baby begins to hold up its head?
sk-d1d02687.explanation: In the fetus the spine is a single C-shaped curve (primary kyphosis). When the baby holds up its head the cervical lordosis develops, and with sitting and walking the lumbar lordosis (secondary curvatures).

sk-b2c190ac.stem: How many pairs of ribs are there in the thoracic cage?
sk-b2c190ac.explanation: Humans have 12 pairs (24) of ribs: 7 pairs of true, 3 pairs of false and 2 pairs of floating ribs.

sk-e3425c63.stem: Which are the 'true ribs', joined directly to the sternum by their own cartilage?
sk-e3425c63.explanation: The true ribs are ribs 1–7. Ribs 8–10 join the cartilage above (false ribs), and the front ends of ribs 11–12 are free (floating ribs).
